learningObject.example: Understanding unique professions such as dog walkers, hotel test sleepers, and food tasters, including their job responsibilities and the benefits or challenges associated with each role.

textContent.description: Reference article used to generate questions
textContent.example: Dog walker Dog walking, as a profession, originated in the US. Some may think that it's a perfect job, because dog walkers won't be imprisoned in an office. But it's actually manual labour. At their busiest, dog walkers may have more than ten dogs to take care of in a day. Hotel test sleeper A hotel test sleeper, as the name suggests, has to write expert reviews about the facilities, locations, prices, dining and other services of hotels, in order to provide evaluations and guides for travelers. Hotel test sleepers don't need to punch in for work and they get about ten thousand yuan as income every month. What a comfortable job! Food taster In ancient times, a food taster was a person who tasted foods (or drinks) to be served to someone else, to confirm that it was safe to eat. But now, those working as food tasters just get to taste various new foods and drinks aimed at specific regions across the world. They then give their opinions on these products to the companies and suggest improvements.

ExecuteAITeacherExpansionDialogue.summary: The expansion exercise dialogues are primarily designed for relatively open-ended communication scenarios. During the exercise, although the questions posed by the AI do not have preset answers, the User must still respond within the relevant topic. If the User’s response deviates from the subject, the AI will attempt to guide them back on topic. If the User goes off-topic twice consecutively, the AI will guide them to proceed to the next topic.

content.example: Ask Mark if he has thought about what his dream job might be.

isOffTopicControl.description:
Indicates whether the conversation is off-topic and serves a flow control purpose.  
This parameter reflects whether the student's response aligns with the dialogue task settings. Its value is derived from the return result of previous dialogue turns. Additionally, this parameter plays a role in flow control.  
If the conversation goes off-topic more than twice, the value is forcibly set to true to trigger a task switch.

prompt.description: An English prompt describing the image to be generated. Replace the role to be generated with <special-token>. For example, change “a man in the snow” to "a <special-token> in the snow" and "a photo of a girl" to "a photo of a <special-token>".

seed.description: Random number seed. When this seed is fixed, the same generated image can be obtained, ensuring reproducibility of the result. Note: The input value must be within the range [-1, 2147483647]. If the input value is outside this range or not provided, a suitable seed will be automatically generated.

strength.description: Indicates the influence strength of the input reference image on the generation process. The valid values are [0.3, 0.4, 0.5, 0.6, 0.7, 0.8]. A smaller value means lower influence from the reference image and correspondingly higher influence from the text prompt. The default value is 0.5, which is suitable for most cases and typically does not require modification.
